text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on October 7 in history.
1471 - Frederick I, King of Denmark who encouraged the spread of Lutheranism in his country, born.

1571 - In the Battle of Lepanto in southwestern Greece, Don John of Austria and his Christian forces defeated the Turkish navy. It was the greatest sea battle since Actium in 31 BC and also the last great confrontation between oared ships.

1728 - U.S revolutionary statesman Ceasar Rodney born. He was a delegate from Delaware to the Continental Congress (1774-76, 1777-78), president of Delaware (1778-81) and key signatory of the Declaration of Independence.
1748 - Charles XIII, King of Sweden from 1809, born. He was the first King of the union of Sweden and Norway.
1763 - George III of Great Britain issued the Proclamation of 1763, closing lands in North America north and west of the Alleghenies to white settlement.
1806 - Carbon paper was patented in London by inventor Ralph Wedgewood.
1849 - Edgar Allan Poe, U.S. writer of mysterious and macabre stories, died aged 40.

1854 - Christiaan Rudolf de Wet born. Boer general and politician. he was commander in chief of the Orange Free State forces in the South African War (1899-1902) and was regarded by Afrikaner nationalists as one of their greatest heroes.
1900 - Heinrich Himmler born. Head of the Nazi Gestapo 1936-45, he was captured by the British and committed suicide on May 23 1945.
1908 - Crete rebelled against Turkish domination and united with Greece.
1912 - Fernando Belaunde Terry born. Peruvian politician, he was president of Peru 1963-68 and 1980-85.
1918 - Sir Hubert Parry, English composer, writer and teacher, famous for "Jerusalem", died aged 70.
1919 - KLM, the national airline of the Netherlands, was established. It is the oldest existing airline.
1931 - Desmond Tutu born. Secretary-General of the South African Council of Churches and leading anti-apartheid campaigner, he won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1984.
1936 - Thomas Keneally born. Australian author and Booker Prize winner for "Schindler's Ark"; the novel was the basis for Steven Spielberg's 1993 film "Schindler's List".
1940 - German troops invade Romania to take control of strategic oilfields. They said they were invited in by the Romanian government to reorganise the army.
1949 - The German Democratic Republic, or East Germany, was proclaimed.
1956 - Clarence Birdseye, inventor of a process to deep freeze food for retailing, died.
1959 - Mario Lanza, U.S. tenor and film actor, died aged 38. His films included "The Great Caruso".
1959 - The far side of the moon was photographed for the first time by the Soviet Union's Luna 3 spacecraft.
1977 - The Soviet Union adopted a new constitution, replacing the one introduced in 1936.

1985 - Palestinian guerrillas seized the Achille Lauro, an Italian passenger ship carrying about 440 people and threatened to blow it up if Israel did not free 50 Palestinian prisoners. Leon Klinghoffer, an elderly wheelchair-bound American, was killed.
1987 - Fiji coup leader Sitiveni Rabuka declared himself head of state of the new republic.
1990 - Sheikh Rashid bin Said al-Maktoum, ruler of Dubai and prime minister and vice-president of the United Arab Emirates, died after a long illness aged 76.
